review_notes: Independently read the entire current proposal.json, functionality.md, both disposition ledgers, coverage.json and unresolved.json. Read canonical and rendered owned source lines 1–425, all 54 subjects and all 60 outgoing links.
All ten proposed writes target owned subjects, use permitted fact types, and are supported by canonical source. The proposal contains no new links, entities, merges or follow-up writes.

Verified foreign definitions for item construction, ownership/status queries, destruction notification, owner detachment, the Kirby holding predicate, installed callbacks, common grounded physics, collision transition helpers, grounded recovery and special-fall setup. The active Kirby table corroborates Hold0/1 callback sharing and grounded startup destination 436.

The current proposal correctly distinguishes nullable construction from guaranteed ownership, fighter-side association from item lifetime, and repeated End animation resets from an independently expiring physics countdown.

The current ledgers conservatively defer section/layout claims, default helplessness, short lockout duration, world-position semantics, transitive cleanup and unsupported runtime tuning. These deferrals are preserved below rather than treated as proved facts.

Independently inspected ftCommon_Fall: it subtracts gravity and clamps self_vel.y only when the result is less than negative terminal velocity. This supports the ordinary terminal-velocity-cap descriptions; exceptional-float gameplay remains deferred.

Collision helpers also change ground/air bookkeeping. In particular, ftCommon_8007D5D4 assigns jumpsUsed = 1, and the air-to-ground path reaches ftCommon_8007D6A4, which assigns jumpsUsed = 0. The proposal's startup jump-write description is correct as an event, not a permanent invariant across collision transitions.
Rendered entry aliases remain hypotheses supported by canonical entry bodies. Rendered external helper aliases were not used as independent evidence.
Acceptance is limited to the submitted proposal and the explicit dispositions below. It does not resolve deferred claims or authorize promotion of them as proved.
